PullRequest.Title: chat: upgrade standalone MCP servers to connectors
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #347211

## Summary

- Keep the existing connector recommendation when no equivalent installation exists.
- Offer an upgrade when an equivalent standalone MCP server is installed, connecting the managed connector before removing matching standalone configurations.
- Suppress recommendations when the connector is already installed or an equivalent MCP server is supplied by a plugin.
- Reconcile the connector catalog after browser authentication so an already-successful connection is not reported as a failure.

## Testing

- `pnpm run compile` — passed
- `.\scripts\test.bat src\vs\workbench\contrib\sessions\test\browser\chat\newChatConnectorRecommendations.test.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\connectorUpgrade.test.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\customizationMarketplaceInstallService.test.ts` — 99 passing
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed
- Targeted ESLint on changed TypeScript files — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

Live-product checks covered normal recommendations and plugin suppression for WorkIQ, plus normal recommendation and standalone upgrade/removal for Slack. Completing the WorkIQ standalone-upgrade and isolated Slack plugin-only authorization paths requires interactive GitHub device authorization.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The input listener calls update directly; unknown inventory calls ensureConnectorInventory, whose finally clears its only guard. The service caches only successful refreshes, and the connector request provider explicitly disables transport coalescing and retries. Failure frequency and response duration are unmeasured, but the repeated-call mechanism is explicit.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Authentication-provider IPC calls and connector-catalog HTTP GET requests, plus associated request/logging work.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For one composer, at most one load is in flight, but the total grows with input/update events after completed failures rather than with account changes or an explicit retry. One matching connector URL suffices; this is not per connector. Multiple composers have independent guards.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive background IPC and network traffic while composing a prompt, consuming request-queue capacity and account/server quota.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Typing after a matching connector URL performed local URL matching and tip construction; the recommendation provider made no authentication or catalog requests.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After an unsuccessful initial catalog load, each subsequent input/layout/inventory event arriving after the prior attempt finishes can initiate another load, with no cooldown or remembered unavailable result.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new update branch at lines 159-161 calls ensureConnectorInventory whenever a URL matches and connectionStateKnown is false; new lines 180-181 call getConnectors and reset _connectorInventoryLoading after every attempt. Previously recommendation updates never requested connector inventory.
Findings.Title: Back off failed connector-inventory loads before retrying on input
Findings.Impact: With recommendations enabled, paste a matching URL and continue typing while the initial catalog is unavailable, for example a non-rate-limit HTTP 403 rollout refusal or repeated network failure. The composer repeatedly probes the same unavailable inventory instead of backing off; signed-out inventory also repeats authentication-session IPC.
Findings.Evidence: newChatConnectorRecommendations.ts:89 subscribes directly to input, :159-161 requests unknown inventory, and :175-185 only guards an active attempt. CopilotConnectorsService.getConnectors (:382-386) uses _lastRefreshTime, which refresh only sets after a successful document (:407-432); unavailable documents retain connectionStateKnown=false. getAuthentication (:827-855) calls authenticationService.getSessions, forwarded to extension-host $getSessions by mainThreadAuthentication.ts:85-87. LocalConnectorsRequestProvider.execute (:66-80) issues GET /plugins through transport with coalesce:false and retry:false; githubTransport.ts:852-856 throws HTTP failures before caching successful representations. Server quota cooldowns still apply, but do not prevent repeated ordinary 403/network-failure probes.
Findings.Recommendation: Remember failed/unavailable inventory attempts and impose a retry cooldown or explicit retry, resetting that state on account/authentication changes. Preserve the existing in-flight guard and successful inventory reuse.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new synchronous call is reached directly on input events. FromEventObservable.get explicitly bypasses caching without observable subscribers, and getInstallationSnapshot performs both mapping passes before its cached-return expression. Nested provider/catalog scans are visible in findKnownResource. Exact latency depends on inventory/catalog sizes and whether another view retains an observable subscription.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UI-thread installation/resource normalization, resource-key serialization, and temporary arrays/objects across all marketplace installations and remembered catalog resources.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: When no other consumer observes installations, there is one complete snapshot callback per matching nondismissed recommendation per input event. For P provider installations and K remembered catalog resources, its provider normalization can scan P×K pairs, with further installation lookups on matches; knownResources retains up to 1,000 catalog entries. One URL and tens of installed customizations after browsing hundreds of catalog entries are sufficient.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Additional synchronous CPU/allocation on the typing path, causing input latency and GC pressure as marketplace inventory grows.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Recommendation input updates matched URLs, selected an ID and constructed a tip without reading or normalizing marketplace installation inventory.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every matching, nondismissed recommendation reads the complete installation snapshot during synchronous input processing, even when both inventory and selected recommendation are unchanged.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: New lines 193-194 add isConnectorInstalled to recommendation filtering, and new line 220 reads installations.get() synchronously. Before this PR the input-driven recommendation update did not enumerate marketplace installations; the previously occasional snapshot-building work is now on every input event with a matching URL.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding marketplace inventory on each input change
Findings.Impact: After browsing marketplace entries, close the customization UI and type a prompt containing a recommended URL with no other installations-observable consumer active, such as with Chat Pet disabled. The warm catalog does not avoid the inventory-normalization work on each edit, so unrelated installed skills/plugins can slow connector recommendations.
Findings.Evidence: newChatConnectorRecommendations.ts:89 invokes update directly on input; :190-195 filters matching recommendations with isConnectorInstalled; :220 calls installations.get(). CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService constructs installations with observableFromEvent at :103. FromEventObservable.get (observableInternal/observables/observableFromEvent.ts:138-149) calls _getValue on every unobserved get. getInstallationSnapshot (:129-140) maps all records and provider installations before `return this.installationSnapshot ??= ...`, so the internal snapshot cache does not skip those passes. Each provider item calls findKnownResource (:220-232), which scans knownResources and performs resource-key/identity comparisons and potentially findProviderInstallation (:277-281). rememberResource bounds knownResources at 1,000 (:203-205), not at the matching connector count.
Findings.Recommendation: Observe installations once and update a connector-identity projection only when that snapshot changes, then use that stable projection during input updates. Alternatively, ensure the snapshot callback returns its cached snapshot before performing normalization; do not rebuild unrelated installation metadata per keystroke.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a new-session composer with an empty/nonmatching prompt, or recommendations disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: NewChatWidget synchronously constructs the recommendation provider and registers its subscriptions. The new plugin observable reads and MCP initial-load access occur regardless of recommendation enablement. Asynchronous MCP enumeration and provider inventory loading are not awaited by composer rendering or prompt submission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize local MCP inventory through mcpManagementService.getInstalled; schedule grouped gallery synchronization afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial query per cold singleton, scanning configured resources; gallery synchronization deduplicates installed server identities by name. No additional initial query per composer when the singleton is warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This recommendation provider did not access the MCP singleton. Other existing composer/workbench consumers could already initialize it, in which case underlying boundary-call count is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started by service initialization; recommendation constructor attaches a continuation rather than awaiting it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Plugin discovery reads manifests/components and maintains filesystem watchers; recommendation autorun observes plugin MCP definitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Discovery is singleton-owned and component observables already recompute initially. Additional recommendation observers do not inherently cause another filesystem read per plugin or keystroke.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The recommendation provider did not observe plugins; the existing plugin service already owned discovery, component reads and watchers for other consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery completion is asynchronous; observer registration and current-plugin iteration are synchronous.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: When the marketplace singleton initializes and an active harness supplies an install provider, list runtime plugins and SDK installation receipts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider refresh per binding/refresh event, shared across composers: plugin inventory followed by receipt inventory, not one IPC per installed item. Registry display-name resolution groups unique unresolved names and caches found/not-found results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The added marketplace-service dependency can bring initialization onto this workflow when cold, but existing customization consumers also initialize the same singleton. It does not create a new inventory service or per-composer backend inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background inventory; not awaited by composer rendering. Cold SDK receipt inventory acquires a shared policy session, then issues three parallel list RPCs, with at most one recovery per affected installation kind.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One recommendation-provider instance per composer, sharing singleton MCP/plugin/marketplace services. Initial discovery scales with installed plugins and configuration resources, not with recommendation count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent initial service work can overlap; plugin/component observation does not add a per-item subprocess. Marketplace provider refreshes are asynchronous/version-guarded; backend SDK list calls use Promise.all. AgentHostManagementService._runMutation tracks operations but is not a serialization lock.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No matching URL means ensureConnectorInventory is not called. MCP/plugin/marketplace state is shared by singleton owners. SDK policy-session creation is coalesced and the session is retained with a ten-minute idle timeout; provider registry-name lookups are claimed before awaiting and cache positive and negative results.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unconditional subscriptions and MCP initial-load access; insufficient evidence that full-workbench startup gains an additional cold singleton initialization rather than reusing existing startup consumers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Which services are already initialized depends on visible workbench surfaces and enabled features. No startup timing was measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate startup finding: the diff adds service access, but incremental expensive initialization on the complete cold-start path was not established independently of existing consumers. Subscription ownership is registered for disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Paste a matching connector URL with unknown inventory, then continue composing through successful, unavailable, or failed catalog loads
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The recommendation waits for catalog state to become known; prompt submission itself does not await this loader. Authentication discovery precedes the catalog HTTP request. Successful catalog publication can update recommendations synchronously before ancillary Agent Host session refresh completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate silent authentication sessions via extension-host $getSessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session-enumeration call per inventory attempt after account initialization; unavailable/signed-out results can repeat after subsequent input events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Recommendation input updates made no authentication-session request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the attempt can discover whether HTTP catalog access is possible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticated GET /plugins through the shared GitHub transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One HTTP request per actual attempt. The provider explicitly sets coalesce:false and retry:false. Ordinary non-rate-limit HTTP failures are not negatively cached; shared server quota cooldowns still apply.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Recommendation updates only matched URLs locally. Catalog requests belonged to existing explicit connector/marketplace consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold recommendation visibility depends on the catalog response; repeated failed probes remain background work during typing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh managed connector configurations in live Agent Host sessions after an authorized catalog/membership transition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One host refresh call for the transition, not one per returned connector. Host providers run concurrently; Copilot marks live sessions and schedules refresh only for eligible idle sessions, coalescing outstanding work per session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session-refresh mechanism existed behind connector catalog refreshes; this PR can reach it from the recommendation's first inventory load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the refresh promise, but catalog state and its change event are published first. Busy sessions defer refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One matching URL is enough. Successful cold loading is one catalog request per composer attempt, not one request per matching connector. On failures, multiplicity follows subsequent update events after completed attempts; multiple composers have independent guards.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one inventory load per composer, with no global loader coalescing across composers. Failures are retried on later events rather than concurrently within one composer. HTTP requests use the shared bounded transport queue and its quota cooldowns.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getConnectors reuses a successful service catalog for 60 seconds; this recommendation provider stops requesting once connectionStateKnown is true. Failed or unavailable initial loads do not set a successful refresh timestamp, and finally clears the only local in-flight guard. Authentication/account changes invalidate catalog context. ETags can revalidate successful representations but do not cache HTTP failures.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: input-to-loader path, success-only cache, guard reset, authentication IPC and noncoalesced HTTP request are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure prevalence and response latency are unmeasured; retry rate is bounded by both event frequency and completion of the previous attempt.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported cache-lifecycle regression: failed/unavailable inventory can repeatedly cross IPC/network boundaries as typing continues.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continue typing with a matching URL after connector inventory is known, with customization views closed and no installations-observable subscriber
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Input events synchronously call update, filter matching recommendations and call isConnectorInstalled before returning to the UI event loop. Inventory normalization occurs before the unchanged-tip state-key early return.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Normalize complete installation inventory, repeatedly compute JSON-stringified resource keys/identities and allocate intermediate arrays and record resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One callback per matching recommendation per input event when installations is unobserved, including with an already-cached installationSnapshot. The mapping/scanning work precedes the cached-return expression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The recommendation's input path did not read installation snapshots or normalize unrelated skills/plugins. Snapshot normalization existed on other less-frequent inventory consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Entirely synchronous on the typing thread. No HTTP, filesystem, database or subprocess call is needed for this warm-path regression.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R matching nondismissed recommendations, P provider installations, K remembered catalog resources (bounded at 1,000), and input/update frequency. A common R=1 still reaches the full marketplace snapshot callback; provider normalization can scan P×K pairs and perform additional installation matching.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded synchronous UI work, with no debounce/coalescing. R snapshot callbacks execute serially within one update.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: FromEventObservable.get caches only while it has an observable subscriber. The new code subscribes to the service event, not to installations itself. With no other observable consumer, every get invokes getInstallationSnapshot; its internal snapshot cache skips final snapshot construction but not preceding mapping and provider/catalog scans. An open observing customization view or enabled observing feature can mask the issue.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: observable implementation, cache-check placement, nested scans and direct input-event call chain are all confirmed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Magnitude depends on installed customization count, remembered catalog entries and whether another feature keeps the observable subscribed; no input latency was measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported repeated-work regression: previously occasional full inventory normalization is materially amplified onto matching-URL keystrokes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Confirm a standalone-MCP-to-connector upgrade, including declining confirmation and preserving changed sources
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Wait for initial MCP inventory, find equivalent installed configurations, take immutable configuration snapshots, and obtain confirmation. After confirmation, resolve the catalog connector, connect/repair and verify installed state, then revalidate and remove each captured source sequentially. Declining confirmation performs no connection or deletion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve connector catalog, authorize, optionally PUT the managed connection and poll GET catalog status until connected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical connector operation for all M sources, not M connections. getConnectors can reuse its 60-second cache; connect refreshes current state and skips PUT if already connected. Polls are serial with a two-second delay and existing five-minute timeout, with bounded authentication-context resets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No upgrade action existed. Users could already invoke the same connector connection/repair mechanisms through marketplace installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All standalone removals wait for successful installation and verification. Browser consent is intentionally on the explicit upgrade critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Preserve shared input references, scan/edit MCP configuration, optionally delete installed server files and refresh local inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: M serial uninstalls. Existing VS Code-format uninstall protection scans up to W other configuration resources in parallel for each source; configuration edits and local inventory refresh follow. Changed/missing captured sources are preserved rather than uninstalled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Standalone deletion used the same single-server uninstall path when explicitly requested; this PR composes those operations into a user-confirmed upgrade.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Explicit upgrade completion waits for cleanup, but the managed connector is already connected. No deletion occurs after an unsuccessful connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Route scoped uninstall to local/shared or remote MCP management service as appropriate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scoped uninstall request per source requiring that boundary, serial across M sources. This is not a per-catalog-entry operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The boundary already served explicit standalone uninstalls; upgrade newly invokes it after successful connector installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before moving to the next source.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M matching standalone configurations after exact case-insensitive alias matching across installation scopes, usually one or a few; W distinct workspace/configuration resources affect existing shared-input protection scans. Plugin matching is in-memory and suppresses recommendations without invoking upgrade.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One connection precedes a serial removal loop. Within an uninstall, shared-input resource scans use Promise.all. Separate command activations are not globally serialized, while existing install operations coalesce by connector key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Local MCP/plugin inventories are read in memory after their initial load; captured source configs are cloned only for the explicit command and compared again before removal. Connector installation deduplicates pending operations by connector key; source snapshots are not retained beyond the command lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for install-before-remove ordering, exact source cardinality, scoped boundary routing and sequential cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cleanup cost depends on number of matching configurations, workspace size and remote filesystem latency. No timings were measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding for the ordinary explicit upgrade scenario: the connection and bounded small-cardinality cleanup are user-requested, ordering is intentional, and source snapshots are command-scoped rather than leaked.

Scenarios.Scenario: A connector installation reports an error after browser authentication, followed by catalog reconciliation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The install catches the connection error and, only for the same initiating account without an authorization-required state, awaits one fresh catalog refresh before accepting an already-connected result or propagating the original error.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-enumerate authentication sessions for the reconciliation refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One enumeration for the additional reconciliation attempt, subject to cancellation/account checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The install propagated the connection-operation failure without this marketplace-layer reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delays final success/error resolution for that install, not normal prompt input.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET/revalidate the connector catalog to establish whether browser authorization actually connected the connector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one additional refresh per caught install failure; no retry loop was added here. Existing ETag revalidation and transport quotas still apply; successful membership changes can invoke the existing grouped Agent Host refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No additional marketplace-layer GET occurred after an unsuccessful connect operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before recording success or rethrowing the original error; a request is bounded by the existing 30-second connector request timeout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One reconciliation per failed logical install operation, independent of standalone-source count. Concurrent callers for the same connector share the install promise; different connector operations can proceed independently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reconciliation is serial after that operation's failure. Same-key installs share one promise; there is no new catalog-wide/per-source fanout or unbounded retry in this branch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: refresh deliberately bypasses the service's 60-second freshness shortcut to obtain authoritative post-authentication state; transport ETags remain usable. Account and authorization conditions are checked before and after the read. The existing per-connector pending map coalesces duplicate install callers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new catch branch performs exactly one conditional refresh and preserves its original error when reconciliation cannot establish success.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Additional error-path latency depends on network response time and how often authentication races occur.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression finding: the additional read is a deliberate, bounded authoritative reconciliation rather than an unnecessary repeated operation. It fixes a correctness race, not a proven prior performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 11 changed files and every diff page in one distinct performance-review pass. Submitted two high-confidence findings: repeated inventory probes after failures/unavailable authentication, and synchronous full installation normalization on matching-URL input events. Traced startup ownership, cold/warm caches, provider/SDK inventory boundaries, connector authentication/polling, Agent Host session refresh, sequential scoped MCP cleanup, and post-error reconciliation. No qualifying performance-regression fix/provenance signal was identified. Static analysis only; no repository code or scripts were executed.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
